headline: Turin, your agentic-AI moment is now—turn the city's industrial-data strengths into a portfolio that hiring managers actually notice.
why_now: GitHub and Hugging Face activity around AI agents is surging (scores 96 and 92) while news mentions and job demand are rising fast (88 and 85). For an agent-focused builder in Turin, where manufacturing and mobility data are abundant, this is the rare window where the tooling, the demand, and the portfolio impact all peak together.
study: Read the LangChain and LlamaIndex agent tutorials end-to-end, then replicate their ReAct and tool-calling examples locally with Ollama.
Build a small function-calling agent in Python using OpenAI/Anthropic APIs plus a vector store (Qdrant or Chroma) over a public Turin dataset (e.g., GTT transit or Piedmont open data).
Study Anthropic's 'Building Effective Agents' and the AutoGen + CrewAI docs to compare single-agent vs. multi-agent orchestration patterns.
Implement one multi-agent workflow (planner + researcher + critic) with CrewAI or AutoGen, instrumenting every step with logging.
Review 2-3 open-source agent repos on GitHub trending in Turin-relevant domains (manufacturing, logistics, mobility) and write notes on their architecture.

build.title: TorinoMobilityAgent
build.description: A multi-agent system that answers natural-language questions about Turin public transit and air quality: a planner agent decomposes the query, a retrieval agent queries Piedmont open-data APIs (GTT, ARPA Piemonte), and a critic agent validates the answer before returning a cited response. It demonstrates tool calling, planning, retrieval-augmented generation, and multi-agent collaboration on a hyper-local dataset that European employers instantly recognize.
deliverables: Public GitHub repo with clean README and architecture diagram
Live Gradio/Streamlit demo deployable on Hugging Face Spaces
Technical write-up (1,000-1,500 words) on Medium or your blog

publish: Post the demo on Hacker News (Show HN) and r/LocalLLaMA with a focused title and a Turin-specific hook.
Submit a talk proposal to the Torino Python Meetup, AI Conf Turin, or an ODSC Europe lightning session.
Cross-post the write-up to LinkedIn tagging Turin tech community accounts and the Piedmont open-data team.
Open-source a reusable 'Italian open-data agent template' so other Italian devs star and fork it, boosting visibility.
skills: Working with public APIs and open-data pipelines
Domain modeling for mobility and environmental data
risks: Open-data APIs for GTT/ARPA can change or rate-limit, so budget time for schema drift and caching.
Multi-agent setups are easy to over-engineer—recruiters value a working single-agent version more than a flaky five-agent one.
GPU/API costs for live demos can spike; pin to small models via Ollama or Hugging Face Inference to keep it free to run.
confidence: Very high—the signals are strong, the local angle is differentiated, and the project is shippable in 2-3 weeks by a focused agent developer.
